archetypes.name: gh-cli
archetypes.rationale: The diff changes GitHub CLI PR creation and recovery semantics where real CLI behavior can diverge from stubs.
archetypes.prompt_body: Investigate the GitHub CLI integration around PR creation, PR lookup, URL recovery, and validation of recovered PRs. Pay special attention to unsupported flags, stdout/stderr URL parsing, repo and branch validation, transient failure handling, and whether tests reflect real gh behavior rather than only mocks. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: git-porcelain
archetypes.rationale: Run-log volatile-only cleanup touches git restore, clean, reset, staging, and dirty-tree invariants before push/merge.
archetypes.prompt_body: Investigate the run-log flush and volatile-only cleanup path for git state safety. Check whether allowlisting is narrow enough, cleanup commands are fail-closed, staging is not left dirty, canonical reports are preserved, and repo-wide porcelain checks match later push and rebase assumptions. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: merge-race
archetypes.rationale: The merge path removes a pre-merge flush and adds PR head OID polling, both of which affect CI convergence and race handling.
archetypes.prompt_body: Investigate merge convergence behavior around removed pre-merge flushing, PR head OID refresh, bounded polling, UNKNOWN merge-state handling, and post-force-push races. Check whether the new behavior preserves bash parity and avoids both stale-head merges and needless extra CI cycles. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: stream-protocol
archetypes.rationale: The Python driver now relies on JSON-only stdout with breadcrumbs routed through stderr or quiet-mode channels.
archetypes.prompt_body: Investigate the stdout, stderr, and quiet-mode protocol for the Python ship driver and CI monitor breadcrumbs. Verify that JSON result emission remains stdout-only across normal, stalled, and internal-error paths, and that breadcrumb routing cannot corrupt machine-readable output or disappear unexpectedly under quiet mode. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: py311-compat
archetypes.rationale: The runtime floor is lowered to Python 3.11 while lint, type, CI, docs, and guards must remain aligned.
archetypes.prompt_body: Investigate Python 3.11 compatibility across packaging metadata, lint and type-checker targets, CI matrix entries, runtime guards, and newly changed Python code. Look for syntax, standard-library, typing, or dependency assumptions that still require Python 3.12 or create inconsistent contributor versus runtime requirements. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: shell-sete
archetypes.rationale: The bootstrap routing parser fix is specifically about set -e behavior in sourced shell helpers.
archetypes.prompt_body: Investigate the shell strict-mode behavior of the bootstrap routing parser and its new harness. Check whether helper return statuses are safe when sourced under set -euo pipefail, especially when values are pre-populated before fallback parsing and when preserve-coder mode changes assignments. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
